Write a company's template package to start from

Source: R/tpl_company.R
tfl_use_company_templates.Rd

A company's templates live in an R package of its own (decided 2026-10-17). This writes one to start from, every file meant to be read and changed: for each template chosen, one tfl_template_variant() call – tflspec's template with the company's defaults, so tflspec's fixes reach it – registered when the package is loaded. It exports nothing: a report's program calls tflspec's tpl_<template>() with the company's defaults written out.

Usage

tfl_use_company_templates(
  path,
  package = basename(path),
  templates = c("demog", "ae_soc_pt"),
  prefix = NULL
)

Arguments

path

The package's folder (made; it must be empty or new).

package

The package's name; the folder's name by default.

templates

tflspec templates to wrap (tfl_templates()).

prefix

The wrapped templates' names are <prefix>_<template> (acme_demog); NULL: package. "": the same names, replacing tflspec's when the package is loaded.

Value

The files written, invisibly.

Details

The files: DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, LICENSE, R/templates.R (the templates), R/zzz.R (their registration), tests/ (that each is registered, takes no look as a parameter and expands), inst/standards/defaults.yml (the company standard a new study's standard is copied from, the form of a study's spec/defaults.yml) and README.md.

Examples

d <- file.path(tempdir(), "acmetpl")
f <- tfl_use_company_templates(d, templates = c("demog", "ae_soc_pt"))
basename(f)
#> [1] "DESCRIPTION"      "LICENSE"          "NAMESPACE"        "templates.R"     
#> [5] "zzz.R"            "testthat.R"       "test-templates.R" "defaults.yml"    
#> [9] "README.md"       
unlink(d, recursive = TRUE)
